title: discardActiveTurn() never marks the in-flight turn settled, so a stale turn clobbers the new one
summary: reset()/restore() call discardActiveTurn(), which nulls activeController/activeTurn but leaves the previous runTurn closure's `settled` flag false. The non-streaming `fallback()` path has no cancellation at all, so when its awaited sdk.text.chat resolves it runs complete() -> conclude(), which nulls activeTurn and sets streaming=false on whatever turn has since replaced it.
failure_scenario: Provider has no chatStream, so send() goes down `fallback()` (line 345) and awaits sdk.text.chat with no controller to cancel. While it is in flight the user clicks another thread in the sidebar -> route watcher -> conversation.restore() -> discardActiveTurn(). The user sends a new message in the restored thread. The old fallback resolves, sees `settled === false`, and runs conclude(): streaming.value=false and activeTurn=null while the NEW turn is still streaming. The Stop button stops cancelling, the composer re-enables mid-stream, and HomePage's persist watcher (keyed on isStreaming going false) writes a half-streamed thread to disk.
recommendation: Expose a per-turn `abort()` from runTurn that sets `settled = true` (and drops the assistant reference), and have discardActiveTurn call it instead of only nulling the module-level handles.

title: send() never resolves when a turn is cancelled via reset()/restore()
summary: runTurn ends with `await finished`, and `finished` is only resolved from conclude(). discardActiveTurn() cancels the StreamController but never calls conclude(), and the StreamController contract guarantees no further data/error/end callbacks fire after cancel(). The promise therefore stays pending forever.
failure_scenario: User sends a message, then navigates to plain /home while it streams. The route watcher calls conversation.reset() -> discardActiveTurn() -> activeController.cancel(). Per StreamController's documented contract ('After cancellation, no more data/error/end callbacks will be invoked', packages/utils/transport/types.ts:158) onEnd/onError never fire, so settle() is never called. `await finished` in runTurn and `await turn` at HomePage.vue:239 stay pending for the life of the window, retaining the whole runTurn closure (handlers, payload, assistant message, parts array) per cancelled turn.
recommendation: Have discardActiveTurn resolve the pending turn (call the same conclude/settle path) rather than only cancelling the transport controller.

title: Conversation route watcher has no in-flight guard: fast sidebar switches restore the wrong thread
summary: The async watcher on route.params.id awaits history.load(target) and then unconditionally assigns conversationId and calls conversation.restore(). Two overlapping invocations are not sequenced, so a slower earlier load overwrites a faster later one.
evidence:
if (target === conversationId) return

    const restored = await history.load(target)
    if (!restored) return
    conversationId = target
    conversation.restore(restored)
failure_scenario: User clicks conversation A then B in the sidebar within a few hundred ms. load(B) resolves first and restores B; load(A) resolves after and restores A while route.params.id is still B. The screen now shows A's messages under URL /home/c/B, and conversationId is A. The next settled turn persists A's thread plus the new turn, then router.replace('/home/c/A') fires because route.params.id !== conversationId — silently rewriting conversation A with content the user typed into what they believed was B.
recommendation: Capture a request token/sequence number before the await and bail if route.params.id has changed by the time load resolves.

title: history.load() rejection in the route watcher is an unhandled rejection with no UI recovery
summary: load() calls sdk.get(id) with no try/catch (unlike its sibling refresh(), which does catch). The only caller is HomePage's async route watcher, which also has no try/catch, so an IPC failure becomes an unhandled promise rejection and the view is left showing the previous thread.
failure_scenario: Main's conversation store is unavailable (DB locked, module not yet loaded, migration in progress). The user opens a stored conversation from the sidebar: sdk.get rejects, the watcher callback rejects, Vue logs an unhandled rejection, conversationId is never updated, and the URL says /home/c/<id> while the stream still renders the previous conversation. No error state is shown and there is no retry affordance.
recommendation: Wrap sdk.get in try/catch returning null (matching refresh()'s degrade-to-empty policy) and surface a load-failed state in HomePage.

title: Tool-confirmation approve/deny rejections are unhandled and permanently drop the request
summary: settle() advances the queue (dismissing the card) before awaiting sdk.decide, and has no catch. HomePage binds it straight to a template handler, so a rejected decide is both an unhandled rejection and an unrecoverable state — the card is gone and the gateway never got an answer.
failure_scenario: Agent tools are on and a tool asks for confirmation. The user clicks Allow; the IPC send fails (transport destroyed during a reload, gateway restarting). advance() has already cleared `pending`, so the TxToolConfirmation card unmounts, but the gateway never receives a decision. The assistant turn hangs on the blocked tool call with no card on screen and no error, and HomePage.vue:712 `@approve="agentTools.approve($event.remember)"` produces an unhandled rejection.
recommendation: Await decide before advancing, or catch and re-queue the request with a visible error so the user can retry.

title: English UI renders raw i18n keys for the capability test input labels
summary: CapabilityTestInput reads four keys under `settings.intelligence.*`, but en-US.json defines them under `settings.settingAISDK.*` and only zh-CN.json has them under `settings.intelligence.*`. English users see the untranslated key path.
failure_scenario: Switch the app to English and open the AI capability test dialog. The two labels render literally as 'settings.intelligence.userMessageLabel' and 'settings.intelligence.promptVariablesLabel', and the two textarea placeholders render as 'settings.intelligence.userMessagePlaceholder' / 'settings.intelligence.promptVariablesPlaceholder', with a vue-i18n 'Not found key' warning per render. Verified: en-US.json has no settings.intelligence.userMessageLabel; the string lives at settings.settingAISDK.userMessageLabel.
recommendation: Move the four keys (userMessageLabel/Placeholder, promptVariablesLabel/Placeholder) from settings.settingAISDK to settings.intelligence in en-US.json, and add a CI check for key-set parity between locales.

title: DivisionBoxShell stays on the loading overlay forever when the initial state request fails
summary: isLoading is set true on mount and only cleared when getState resolves with an active state or a later stateChanged event says 'active'. The .catch() only logs, so a failed or non-success response leaves the shell permanently in its loading state with no error affordance.
failure_scenario: The DivisionBox session is torn down in main between window creation and the shell's getState call (or the transport send times out). The catch logs and returns; isLoading stays true and no stateChanged event for this sessionId ever arrives, so the user is left staring at 'Loading...' with no close path from within the shell.
recommendation: Clear isLoading in the catch and in the non-success branch, and render an error state with a retry/close action.

title: Search snapshot overwrites the established session id with an optional field, stranding loading=true
summary: The stream's `session` chunk sets currentSearchId correctly, then the snapshot handler unconditionally reassigns it from `initialResult.sessionId`, which is declared optional on TuffSearchResult. When that field is absent the id becomes null and every later chunk fails its `currentSearchId.value === chunk.sessionId` guard.
failure_scenario: A provider returns a TuffSearchResult without `sessionId` (the field is `sessionId?: string` in packages/utils/core-box/tuff/tuff-dsl.ts:1485, and applyDetachedPayload at useSearch.ts:335 constructs exactly such a result). currentSearchId flips to null after the snapshot, so the later `update` chunks (line 996) and the `complete` chunk (line 1011) are both dropped by their session guards. applySearchEnd never runs, so `loading.value` is never set back to false: the CoreBox spinner runs forever, streaming results stop appearing, and CoreBox.vue:150 keeps `canSubmitFeaturePrompt` false so the send button stays disabled until the box is closed.
recommendation: Only reassign when the snapshot actually carries an id (`if (initialResult.sessionId) currentSearchId.value = initialResult.sessionId`), and set loading=false on the snapshot path as a backstop. Same fix needed at line 930 in applyRecommendationResult.

title: Store plugin cards are unreachable by keyboard — click-only <div> with no role or tabindex
summary: The entire plugin card is a plain <div> carrying the only affordance that opens plugin details. It has no role, no tabindex, and no keydown handler, so it is not focusable and does not respond to Enter/Space.
failure_scenario: A keyboard-only or screen-reader user opens the plugin store and tabs through the grid. No card ever receives focus, and a screen reader announces each card as an unlabelled group rather than a control, so plugin detail pages cannot be opened at all without a mouse. The install button inside is focusable, meaning the only reachable action is installing a plugin whose details the user cannot read.
recommendation: Make the card a <button>/<a>, or add role="button", tabindex="0" and @keydown.enter/@keydown.space handlers.

title: Store source delete control is a click-only <div>, unreachable by keyboard
summary: The destructive 'remove source' affordance is a bare <div> with only @click, in both the list branches (lines 235-238 and 284-287). No role, tabindex, keydown handler, or accessible name.
failure_scenario: A keyboard user configuring plugin store sources tabs to the row: the enable/disable switch takes focus but the delete control never does, so a mis-added source cannot be removed without a mouse. A screen reader reads only the icon <div> with no accessible name, giving no indication that a destructive action exists there.
recommendation: Use <button type="button"> with :disabled and an aria-label for the delete affordance in both branches.

title: WidgetFrame shadow render mode can never mount: pre-flush watcher reads the template ref too early
summary: mountShadowApp() is driven by a default (pre-flush) watcher with immediate: true, but it needs shadowHost.value, which Vue only populates after the render that creates the `v-else-if="canRenderShadow"` div. ensureShadowRoot() therefore returns null and mountShadowApp bails, and nothing re-triggers the watcher afterwards.
failure_scenario: Pass render-mode="shadow" to WidgetFrame with a registered renderer. On the immediate run the component is not mounted, so shadowHost.value is null; ensureShadowRoot() returns null and mountShadowApp() returns at `if (!root || !shadowContainer.value) return`. On the async path (renderer registers later) canRenderShadow flips false->true, but the pre-flush watcher still runs before the div is patched in, so shadowHost.value is null again. The result is an empty .WidgetFrame-ShadowHost div with no widget in it and no error. Currently latent — no caller passes render-mode="shadow" (only the 'light' default is used by CoreBoxRender.vue:71 and PluginFeatureDetailCard.vue:751), so ~100 lines of shadow-DOM plumbing are dead and untested.
recommendation: Add `flush: 'post'` to the watcher (or move mountShadowApp into onMounted + a post-flush watcher), and either wire up a caller or delete the shadow path.

title: forTouchTip atomicKey is poisoned permanently if the dialog fails to render
summary: The atomic entry is only removed inside the dialog's close callback. If the promise executor throws — renderComponent throws when no app context has been captured — the rejected promise is still stored under atomicKey and every later call with that key returns the same rejected promise instead of showing a dialog.
failure_scenario: forTouchTip is called with an atomicKey from a non-Vue context (an IPC callback or a DOM listener) before captureAppContext() has run — renderComponent throws 'No app context available' at line 126. The executor's throw rejects `pending`, which is then stored in activeAtomicDialogs and never deleted because close() is never reached. The empty root <div> also stays appended to document.body. Every subsequent forTouchTip with that key hits `if (activeDialog) return activeDialog` and re-throws the same stale rejection, so that dialog can never be shown again for the life of the window.
recommendation: Attach a `.catch()` / `.finally()` to `pending` that removes the atomicKey entry and the root element, and register the entry before mounting so a synchronous close still cleans up.

title: agentTools.setEnabled() is fire-and-forget: the pill can show 'on' while the gateway never opened
summary: The computed setter writes the persisted flag and then calls the async main-process sync with `void`, discarding both the result and any rejection. There is no rollback and no error surface.
failure_scenario: User clicks the agent-tools pill. `appSetting.tools.agentTools` is set to true and persisted, but sdk.setEnabled rejects (gateway port in use, main handler not registered). The rejection is an unhandled promise rejection, the pill renders as active and `aria-pressed="true"`, and the setting survives a restart — so the UI permanently claims the assistant can run tools while the tool gateway is closed and every tool call the model attempts fails.
recommendation: Await the call in an async handler; on failure revert appSetting.tools.agentTools and show a toast.

title: Cancelled route transitions leak entries in AppShell's timing map
summary: routeTransitionStartedAt is filled in @before-enter and only drained in @after-enter. Vue fires @enter-cancelled (not @after-enter) when a transition is interrupted, and that hook is not bound, so interrupted navigations leave entries behind forever.
failure_scenario: The key is route.fullPath, and conversation routes are /home/c/<uuid> — an unbounded key space. A user clicking quickly through the conversation sidebar interrupts the 0.35s route transition each time, so @after-enter never fires and one entry per visited conversation id accumulates in the Map for the life of the window. AppShell is the root layout and never unmounts, so nothing ever clears it.
recommendation: Bind @enter-cancelled to the same cleanup, or cap/clear the map when it exceeds a small size.
